    How it works

    Three steps, either side of the table

    1

    Find food by ZIP

    Browse permitted kitchens near you. Every listing shows the dish, the price, the pickup window — and the kitchen’s MEHKO permit number.

    2

    Order & pay — held, not charged through

    Your payment is held while the chef confirms they can cook it. If they can’t accept, you’re not out the money.

    3

    Pick it up

    The pickup address is released only after the chef accepts your order. You collect it yourself — hometable is pickup only, with no delivery.

    1

    Get permitted first

    Hold a valid San Diego County MEHKO permit and food-safety certification before anything is published. No permit, no listing — no exceptions.

    2

    Publish your menu

    Set your dishes, prices and pickup windows within the legal caps — up to 30 meals a day and 90 meals a week. hometable reviews and approves your kitchen before it goes live.

    3

    Cook, hand off, get paid

    Accept orders, cook, and hand the food to the customer at pickup. Payouts run through Stripe Connect, minus the fee stated plainly below.

    Fees — stated clearly, as the law requires

    What it costs. All of it, up front.

    California law requires an IFSI to clearly state the fees for its services on its website. Here they are — the same numbers a customer and a chef both see.

    WhoFeeWhat it means
    Chefs — Year 1 introductory5% of each orderThe launch rate for founding chefs in their first year on hometable.
    Chefs — standard10% of each orderThe normal platform commission after the introductory period.
    Chefs — future, only if demand proves itUp to 15%Not charged today. It would only ever apply later, if demand is proven, and would be announced before it changes.
    CustomersThe dish priceYou pay the price on the listing. Pickup is free — there is no delivery to charge for.
    hometable keeps / chef receives$0.93 / $17.57Before payment-processing costs. Try the $18.50 average ticket.

    For home chefs

    Cook from your own kitchen. Earn from your own table.

    hometable exists so home cooks can earn household income legally — under a MEHKO permit, inside the caps, with the rules explained before your first dish is ever published. Informing you of those requirements is one of our legal duties as an IFSI, and this page is part of how we do it.

    • ✓

      A valid MEHKO permit from San Diego County for your home kitchen — obtained before you list, and your permit number displayed on your kitchen page.

    • ✓

      Food-safety certification current and on file with hometable before approval.

    • ✓

      Your consent to disclose — as an IFSI we must have your consent to share your name and permit number with government agencies when the law requires it, including the complaint rule below.

    • ✓

      Approval before you appear — new kitchens stay hidden until hometable reviews and approves them.

    • ✓

      Pickup only, from your handoff point — customers collect their order; there is no delivery and no third-party delivery service.

    30meals per day, max
    90meals per week, max
    $110,442gross per year, max (2026)

    The caps are the law’s, not ours — growth comes from more chefs and more counties, not from any one kitchen cooking past them.

    Safety, complaints & insurance

    If something’s wrong with your food, here’s exactly what to do

    An IFSI must conspicuously post how a consumer can report a food-safety complaint. This section stays on the live page, in this position — it is not fine print.

    Report a food-safety concern

    1 · To hometable

    Use the “Report a food-safety concern” option on your order in the app, or from any kitchen page. Tell us the kitchen, the dish, and what happened. Every report is logged.

    2 · To San Diego County directly

    You can always go straight to the regulator: San Diego County Department of Environmental Health and Quality (DEHQ), the local enforcement agency for MEHKO permits.

    2 complaintsFood-safety warning to the kitchen, with a review of what went wrong.
    3 complaintsThe kitchen is blocked from selling while the matter is reviewed.
    3+ unrelated, in 2 weeksBy law, hometable reports the kitchen’s name and permit number to the local enforcement agency.

    Service problems (late, cold, wrong order) follow a separate ladder — warning at 3, block at 5 — and never substitute for the food-safety route above.

    Liability insurance — open item, posted here before launch. California law requires an IFSI to conspicuously post its liability insurance information on its website. The carrier and policy details go in this box, on this page, before hometable takes its first order. The quote is still outstanding, so no insurer is named here yet — inventing one would be worse than the gap.

    What “IFSI” means — and why registration comes first

    An Internet Food Service Intermediary (IFSI) is an entity that facilitates the sale of home-cooked meals offered by microenterprise home kitchen operations (MEHKOs) through a web or mobile platform. IFSIs have responsibilities under Chapter 11.6 of the California Retail Food Code and must register with the California Department of Public Health. Rule zero for hometable: registration comes before advertising or promoting any MEHKO — not just before the first order.

    Registration is filed on CDPH Form 9144, under the company (LLC) name once formed, with the Food and Drug Branch — Retail Food Program, California Department of Public Health, P.O. Box 997435, MS 7602, Sacramento, CA 95899-7435. Background: mehko.org — Internet Food Service Intermediaries.

    For the build — Dinesh & Avinash

    What this draft is asking the real app to do

    Everything above is customer-facing copy. This section is the spec behind it — the rules the Fastify / Postgres / Stripe Connect build has to enforce, taken from the agreed design.

    Every kitchen page must carry

    • Permit-number field — dedicated, required, blocks publishing when empty
    • Kitchen ID (e.g. CHF-101), ZIP, pickup windows, live / hidden state
    • New enrollments hidden until admin approval
    • Complaint entry point on the page itself

    Order flow rules

    • Lock the inventory row when an order is placed — that’s what enforces the caps
    • Payment intent on hold, not charged through, until the chef accepts
    • Pickup address released only after acceptance
    • Idempotency keys on order creation; Stripe stays server-side only

    Caps & ladders, in the data

    • 30 / day, 90 / week per chef, enforced — not displayed and hoped for
    • Food safety: warn at 2, block at 3 · Service: warn at 3, block at 5
    • 3+ unrelated food-safety complaints in 2 weeks → report name + permit # to DEHQ
    • Audit log for every action — blocks, money and disclosures are human-approved

    Never in the product

    • The word “catering” — not in copy, plans, or metadata
    • No third-party delivery — the only exception is the disability exception in the rules
    • No promoting a specific MEHKO before IFSI registration is complete
    • No kitchen goes live without permit + consent-to-disclose on file

    Fees, in code as on this page

    • Commission is a stated config value: 5% intro → 10% standard
    • 15% exists only as a future, announced change — never a silent default
    • The fee shown at checkout must match this page, word for word

    Open items before launch

    • LLC formed → IFSI registration on Form 9144 under the LLC name
    • Liability insurance bound → details posted in the Safety section above
    • Chef agreement checked for the explicit consent-to-disclose clause
    • Founder’s own MEHKO permit (Track 2) before his kitchen lists

    Questions, answered plainly

    Is hometable a delivery service?

    No. hometable is pickup only. You collect your order from the chef’s handoff point yourself, and no third-party delivery service is used.

    Are the kitchens inspected businesses?

    Each kitchen is a microenterprise home kitchen operation (MEHKO) — a home kitchen permitted by San Diego County under California law, subject to its permit conditions and caps. The permit number appears on every kitchen page.

    Can I order today?

    Not yet. This is a draft landing page for the build. Orders open only after hometable’s IFSI registration is complete, its insurance information is posted, and each kitchen’s permit is verified — in that order.

    I cook at home. What do I need before I can sell?

    A valid MEHKO permit and current food-safety certification first, then hometable’s review and approval, and your consent for us to disclose your name and permit number to government agencies when the law requires it. The full list is in the For chefs section above.

    What does hometable charge?

    Chefs pay 5% of each order in their introductory first year and 10% standard after that. Customers pay the dish price on the listing. The full fee table is in the Fees section above.
